Gender Discrimination Gender discrimination means the discriminatory (বৈষম্যমুলক) distribution of rights between male and female on the basis of gender identity (পরিচিতি). Unfortunately the female children are the worst victims of gender discrimination which begins at their birth. It is a matter of great regret (অনুশোচনা) that it continues till death. Social prejudices (পÿপাতিত্ব), customs and our male domination trend are all the major causes of it. Religious misinterpretation (ধমীর্য় অপব্যাখ্যা) contributes to the degradation (অবনতি) of women's position in the society. The birth of a female child is unwelcomed because it is thought as a burden by the parents. So, from the very early stage parents take more care in all respects for the male children. Gender discrimination is undoubtedly harmful to female gender causing their health hazard (বিপযর্য়), mental distress and even in some cases causing their death. Being deprived of proper health care and nutrition they become vulnerable to various diseases. They are considered as half-human beings who are born only to become wife of a husband and the mother of some children. This critical position makes them victim of all evil things like dowry, illiteracy, malnutrition etc. To resolve this problem we should change our outlook towards girls. It should be established that women are equal partners to men. Proper education and nutrition should be rendered to female children. This social curse of gender discrimination will be cured only when we will realize that women are human beings than mere women.
source: SSC English 1st Paper Test Paper 111 — Barisal Govt. Girls' High School
